entries.title: Exact near-critical percolation amplitude on a regular tree
entries.statement: For independent bond percolation on the infinite d-regular tree with d>=3, p_c=1/(d-1), theta(p)=0 for p<=p_c, and theta(p)=[2d(d-1)/(d-2)](p-p_c)+O((p-p_c)^2) as p decreases to p_c from above. The positive descendant-survival solution u obeys 1-u=(1-pu)^(d-1); division by u and the implicit-function theorem give the expansion, and theta=1-(1-pu)^d. This is an exact tree analogue, not a high-dimensional lattice solution.
entries.proof_text:
The cached Heydenreich-van der Hofstad source's Open Problem 9.1 asks for a positive limit of theta(p)/(p-p_c) for high-dimensional lattice percolation, beyond bounded ratios. The intake route writes beta=gamma-Delta while substituting gamma=1 and Delta=2; that displayed subtraction cannot produce beta=1. We do not accept the claimed equivalence or differentiation of a singular limit as proved.

For bond percolation on the infinite d-regular tree, d>=3, p_c=1/(d-1) and

    theta(p) = [2d(d-1)/(d-2)] (p-p_c)+O((p-p_c)^2).

Let k=d-1 and u be the probability that a vertex with its parent edge removed has an infinite descendant cluster. It solves 1-u=(1-pu)^k. For p>1/k it is the positive branching-process survival solution. Dividing by u and expanding gives kp-1=binom(k,2)p^2 u+O(u^2). The divided equation has nonzero u derivative at (u,p)=(0,1/k), so its positive branch is analytic. With epsilon=p-1/k, u=2k^2 epsilon/(k-1)+O(epsilon^2), and theta=1-(1-pu)^d gives the claimed coefficient. This is a tree analogue, not a proof on Z^d. Nine small numerical checks for d=3,4,8 approach the predicted slopes.

Bounded-ratio exponent information and monotonicity alone are insufficient: F(epsilon)=epsilon(2+sin(log epsilon)), epsilon>0 small, lies between epsilon and 3epsilon and is strictly increasing because F'=2+sin(log epsilon)+cos(log epsilon)>=2-sqrt(2)>0. Nevertheless F(epsilon)/epsilon has no limit, while log F/log epsilon ->1. A lattice-percolation proof therefore needs an additional mechanism ruling out oscillation; this example is not a percolation counterexample.

entries.title: Monotonicity and exponent one do not force a limiting amplitude
entries.statement: On 0<epsilon<1/4, F(epsilon)=epsilon(2+sin(log epsilon)) is strictly increasing, lies between epsilon and 3epsilon, and satisfies log F(epsilon)/log epsilon ->1 as epsilon tends to zero. Nevertheless F(epsilon)/epsilon has no limit. Thus monotonicity plus bounded-ratio beta=1 alone cannot establish asymptotic equivalence to c epsilon. This analytic counterexample is a refuted inference, not a percolation counterexample.

entries.title: The archived beta equals gamma minus Delta route does not establish beta one
entries.statement: The C0063-A001 intake attempt displays beta=gamma-Delta with gamma=1 and Delta=2 and claims that this gives beta=1. The displayed arithmetic instead gives -1. This records a route failure in that attempt and does not assert a replacement scaling theorem or equivalence of unresolved amplitude statements. Singular-limit differentiation and a right derivative at criticality still require proof for the requested lattice model.
